newsitem.title: USA: Florida's Graham to try again for Senate.
newsitem.headline: Florida's Graham to try again for Senate.

text.p: Florida Democratic Sen. Bob Graham said Monday he will seek re-election to the Senate in 1998 in hopes of bolstering the party's moderate centre.
Graham, a moderate, had been considering leaving the Senate at the end of his current term to seek election as Florida's governor.

"I have concluded that I can be of the greatest service to the people of this state in the period after 1998 by continuing to serve in the United States Senate," he told a small crowd of relatives and supporters at an elementary school in a poor area near Miami.
Democratic Gov. Lawton Chiles will retire at the end of his term in 1998. Graham, a popular figure in Florida who was governor for two terms from 1978 to 1986, turned 60 Saturday.

Some political pundits said Graham was the only Democrat who could win the governorship, but he said he decided he should remain in the Senate to strengthen the centre following the resignations of several moderates, such as Democrat Bill Bradley of New Jersey, Republican Nancy Kassebaum of Kansas, and Democrat Sam Nunn of Georgia.
"I believe that it is important that moderate Republicans and moderate Democrats step forward and provide leadership," Graham said.

He said he was pleased that Congress and the White House had worked together more effectively in 1996, in contrast with the year following the 1994 election which saw control of Congress pass from the Democratic to the Republican party.

"1995 was not a good year to serve in Congress. It was characterised by bitterness, ideological combat and a lack of much performance on things that were important to the people of the country," Graham said. "1996 was a much better year."

Graham's decision not to run seemed to pave the way for a 1998 gubernatorial battle pitting Jeb Bush, son of former President George Bush, against Lt.-Gov. Buddy MacKay, who has said he will run for governor when Chiles retires.
Bush, a Miami-area businessman, lost narrowly to Chiles in 1994.
